title: Prospero Redesigns the Milan Island Network
context_md:
Prospero, Network Architect at *Milan Island Telecom*, is dismantling the company's twenty-year-old castle-and-moat network. After the pandemic, two-thirds of the workforce became permanent remote, contractors connect from a dozen countries, and the company adopted three SaaS suites — none of which sit behind the corporate firewall.

The legacy design assumes that anyone inside the perimeter VPN is trustworthy. Prospero has been asked to fix this without forcing every remote worker to backhaul traffic through the Milan headquarters, which would crush the WAN links and add 200ms of latency to every Salesforce request.

His plan: collapse networking and security functions into a single cloud-delivered edge service, evaluate every request continuously rather than once at login, break the flat internal network into per-application segments small enough that a single compromised laptop cannot reach the customer billing database, and classify all data so that DLP rules can travel with files even when they leave the network.

Prospero also has to convince the auditors that he can *measure* whether the new controls work — not just claim they do.
artifact_title: Architecture Review — Milan Island Telecom (auditor's working table)
artifact_md:
| Domain | Today | Pain point observed |
|---|---|---|
| **Workforce** | 67% permanent remote; contractors in 12 countries | n/a (driver, not finding) |
| **WAN path** | All remote traffic backhauled → Milan HQ VPN concentrator | +200 ms to every Salesforce request; users tunneling around VPN |
| **Internal segmentation** | Flat /16; customer billing DB reachable from any VPN-authenticated laptop | Lateral movement trivial — confirmed in March red-team |
| **Authorization model** | Identity checked once at VPN login | Stolen session ≈ stolen tenure; no posture re-check |
| **Customer data** | No labels, no DLP at egress, no scanning at rest | Auditor pulled 47 mislabeled customer files in 20 minutes |
| **Effectiveness reporting** | Quarterly slide: *"controls are in place"* | No measurable evidence; auditors flagged on last review |
prompt_md: Map each row of the audit table to Prospero's Zero Trust fix, then click **Check answers**.
body_md:
The *Workforce* + *WAN path* rows drive the access layer: Prospero will replace the hub-and-spoke VPN with a **{{edge_service}}** that delivers SD-WAN, SWG, CASB, ZTNA, and FWaaS from cloud points of presence close to the user, eliminating the backhaul penalty.

Rather than trusting the network location of a request, every access decision will be made at a **{{pdp}}**, which evaluates identity, device posture, and context. The decision is then enforced at the **{{pep}}** in front of each application. The *Authorization* row is fixed by making authorization **{{auth_model}}** — re-evaluated on every request, not granted once at login.

The *Internal segmentation* row is fixed by **{{segmentation}}** — far finer-grained than traditional VLAN segmentation. A compromised endpoint can reach only the services it has been explicitly authorized for.

The *Customer data* row is fixed in three moves: every customer file is assigned a sensitivity **{{label}}** at creation, **{{dlp_state}}** DLP rules scan email and SaaS uploads for matching content as it leaves the environment, and files at rest are inspected by **{{discovery}}** scans to find mislabeled or shadow copies.

The *Effectiveness reporting* row is fixed by publishing a quarterly dashboard of **{{metric}}** — quantitative evidence that the controls reduce real risk, not just compliance checkboxes.

edge_service.explanation: SASE is the cloud-delivered convergence of SD-WAN with security services (SWG, CASB, ZTNA, FWaaS) — purpose-built for the deperimeterized, remote-first scenario described.

pdp.explanation: In Zero Trust architecture, the PDP evaluates context and produces an authorization decision; the PEP enforces that decision at the resource.

pep.explanation: The PEP sits in the data path and applies the PDP's allow/deny decision to the actual request.

auth_model.explanation: Continuous authorization (re-evaluating identity, device posture, and context on every request) is the core Zero Trust principle distinguishing it from traditional perimeter or session-based models.

segmentation.explanation: Microsegmentation creates per-workload (often per-process) policy boundaries — the granularity needed to limit east-west movement after compromise. VLANs operate at far coarser scope.

label.explanation: Data classification labels (e.g., Public / Internal / Confidential / Restricted) travel with the data and let DLP and access controls apply consistent rules across systems.

dlp_state.explanation: Email and SaaS-upload inspection happens as data moves — DLP for data *in transit*. At-rest DLP scans stored files; in-use DLP watches endpoints during active editing.

discovery.explanation: Data discovery scans repositories for sensitive content, detecting mislabeled, shadow, or forgotten copies of regulated data.

metric.explanation: Auditors and the board want measurable evidence that controls work — coverage %, mean-time-to-detect, blocked vs. allowed event ratios, etc. Effectiveness metrics convert security claims into defensible numbers.
